strengths: The task addresses a meaningful gap: identifying, segmenting and maintaining identities of sounding instances, including multiple objects from the same category. AVISeg provides a substantial resource with 926 videos, 94,074 masks, 26 categories and an average duration of 61.4 seconds. The benchmark contribution and supporting results favor weak acceptance despite the reservations below.

The baseline shows consistent improvements on established metrics, independently of the proposed FSLA metric. Under the stated matched ResNet-50 and training-iteration protocol, Table 2 reports HOTA/mAP of 61.73/40.57, compared with 57.48/36.25 for VITA and 57.39/37.84 for COMBO.

The ablations provide useful evidence for the audio-fusion components. In Table 4, adding frame-level fusion increases HOTA from 57.48 to 59.59, and adding video-level fusion increases it to 61.73. Additional experiments examine window size, pretraining, backbone capacity and similarity loss.

The supplement supplies optimization settings, query counts, prediction thresholds and large-model prompts, alongside qualitative comparisons and explicit failure cases. The manuscript provides a dataset/code URL, supporting potential reuse. :codex-file-citation{path="/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b03/review-experiment-xi1rl17_/call-78828bc292de4216b31667a6f1200d6e/manuscript.pdf" purpose="source"}
weaknesses: FSLA has a substantive specification problem. Supplementary Algorithm 1 increments the silent-frame correctness counter without checking predictions, initializes counters outside the IoU-threshold loop without resetting them, and omits explicit checks for exact object count and correctness of every instance. Its aggregation also does not implement the stated class averaging. Consequently, the reported FSLA results cannot be reproduced from this pseudocode. This does not establish that the actual implementation or separate HOTA/mAP results are incorrect. Additionally, the statement that mAP does not decrease for nonsounding predictions is too broad: such false positives can reduce AP depending on their ranking.

The conclusions about multimodal large models exceed what the evaluation establishes. Sections E.1-E.2 merge same-category masks into one object, E.4 treats each category as one instance, and the Sam4AVS adaptation selects only the highest-scoring audio class. These choices structurally restrict success on the central multiple-instance problem. PG-Video-LLaVA also receives speech transcripts that omit nonspeech audio information. Table 3 therefore demonstrates limitations of these particular zero-shot pipelines, without isolating the underlying models' instance discrimination or temporal reasoning capabilities.

Dataset quality assurance is insufficiently documented for the hardest annotation decision: determining which individual object produced a sound. Section 4 describes SAM-assisted masks and repeated manual review, but provides no agreement measurements or detailed adjudication rules for ambiguous same-category sources, off-screen sounds, or sound transitions within one-second snippets. These uncertainties concern the benchmark's target labels, beyond mask-boundary quality.

The experiments only partially establish the central same-category and long-range capabilities. Results are not stratified by simultaneous same-category sources, temporal separation or video length, although Figure 10 identifies same-category attribution as a recurring failure. Table 5 measures window-size effects and maximum frame capacity, rather than accuracy over increasingly long dependencies or comparative runtime. With 1 FPS sampling and 539 of 926 videos involving music, the evidence supports a narrower operating scope than the broad real-world motivation.

Architectural originality is modest. Object-token compression, association, shifted-window processing and much of the training formulation follow Mask2Former/VITA; the principal adaptation is audio fusion at two levels. This is reasonable for a benchmark baseline, but the strongest acceptance argument rests on the task and dataset rather than a substantially new segmentation architecture.
